Finite-order phases and missing powers

If the first nonzero derivative of a real phase has order , its natural spatial scale is . Taylor coefficients of the transformed amplitude then produce powers of , but some coefficients vanish for geometric reasons. An even monomial phase kills every odd amplitude jet. An odd monomial phase has a different cancellation: jets whose degree plus one is divisible by make no contribution. The cubic case connects these cancellations with the Airy equation.

We use The amplitude is initially a Schwartz function. Local applications use compact smooth amplitudes. Pairings are complex bilinear, and .

Polynomial phases and Fourier tails, Theorem B, proves that the Fourier transform of every real polynomial exponential of degree at least two has an entire representative. On the real axis its bound (B9) is ; in degree two the explicit Gaussian is bounded. Solution 8 proves convergence of Gaussian regularization with every complex-frequency derivative.
